Robinhood upgraded, Uber initiated: Wall Street's top analyst calls

The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.

Top 5 Upgrades:

Morgan Stanley upgraded Robinhood (HOOD) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $150, up from $124. The firm sees increasing evidence that Robinhood's broader product capabilities are improving the economics of its installed customer base, supporting more assets per customer.

Evercore ISI upgraded Duolingo (DUOL) to Outperform from In Line with a price target of $210, up from $105, after "materially increasing" the firm's estimates in the wake of a proprietary survey and an analysis of current product improvements.

Piper Sandler upgraded Akamai (AKAM) to Overweight from Neutral with a price target of $125, down from $140. The Compute segment is about to show a "material inflection" and should show an acceleration as Akamai can show it is benefitting from AI builds and the pipeline is "robust," the firm tells investors.

Piper Sandler upgraded Tempus AI (TEM) to Overweight from Neutral with a price target of $76, up from $56. The pending acquisition of Personalis (PSNL) gives Tempus ownership of a differentiated tumor-informed molecular residual disease platform, the firm tells investors in a research note.

BofA upgraded Timken (TKR) to Buy from Neutral with a price target of $135, up from $129. Shares are down 17% post Q2 results, notes the firm, which believes this "sets up an entry point into a multi-year transformation story."

Top 5 Downgrades:

Piper Sandler double downgraded Myriad Genetics (MYGN) to Underweight from Overweight with a price target of $2, down from $5.45. Piper does not believe Myriad's current business model can grow or cut its way to profitability.

BofA downgraded Edison International (EIX) to Neutral from Buy with a price target of $51, down from $81. A "once-in-a-generation reform opportunity" falls short of expectations and leaves a less compelling risk reward, the firm tells investors.

BofA downgraded PG&E (PCG) to Neutral from Buy with a price target of $13, down from $24. California bill SB 492 fails to address the wildfire financing risks facing utilities, the firm tells investors in a research note.

BMO Capital downgraded Xenia Hotels (XHR) to Market Perform from Outperform with a price target of $20.50, down from $22. The firm says the company has "fewer differentiated catalysts" relative to peers in 2027 following a strong 2026.

Morgan Stanley downgraded Miami International (MIAX) to Equal Weight from Overweight with a price target of $50, down from $53. The company's near-term risk/reward is more balanced following its market share rebounding to high teens in Q3, the firm tells investors in a research note.

Expanding Service Model Drives New Leadership Roles

FAIRHOPE, Ala., September 01, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aptus Capital Advisors ("Aptus") welcomes Joshua Lucas, Tom Winkler and John Davenport to key leadership roles as the firm scales its options-based ETF and custom overlay businesses.

Founded in 2013, Aptus supports advisors in portfolio design, due diligence and documentation, and client acquisition and messaging. The addition of LibertyFi in 2023 built on the firm's ability to blend investment management, technology and operations into an integrated solution.

Joshua Lucas joins as Head of Digital Strategy. He was previously Chief Operating Officer at Scalio, a digital product studio that built custom software for clients including Google, Uber and Airbnb.

Tom Winkler, CIMA®, CETF® joins as Head of Wealth and Client Solutions. He brings a career spent helping professional allocators make portfolio decisions on behalf of their clients.

John Davenport, PhD, MBA joins as Head of Client Specialists, where he will lead the Aptus Consulting Team in helping advisors deliver the enhanced client experience we've supported for our wealth management partners.

"Our bread and butter is helping advisors improve outcomes for clients — through ownership of more growth assets, and through the communication that keeps clients confident in every kind of market," said JD Gardner, Founder of Aptus Capital Advisors. "John and Tom know how to help advisors evaluate portfolio decisions and build durable processes for running an enterprise. Joshua brings digital expertise that can extend our reach and give advisors direct access to client acquisition and management tools. We're thrilled to add experienced folks who understand the value of tech-empowered partners in doing daily work for advisors and their clients."

For more information about Aptus Capital Advisors, please visit: https://aptuscapitaladvisors.com/

About Aptus Capital Advisors

Aptus Capital Advisors, an SEC-registered investment adviser, specializes in options-based ETFs and helps advisors grow and manage a confident client base. Its mission is to help independent wealth managers pursue better client outcomes, building on their financial planning with thoughtful portfolio design and clear communication. As of June 30, 2026, the firm managed $14.2 billion in total assets under management, including $6.6 billion in ETF assets.

title: Jim Cramer Says Stay Long Airbnb Stock (ABNB) Despite Fee Concerns
detail:
Jim Cramer Says Stay Long Airbnb Stock (ABNB) Despite Fee Concerns
Syeda Seirut Javed
Fri, August 28, 2026 at 1:21 PM PDT 3 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

A caller on the August 26 episode of Mad Money highlighted local neighbors abandoning Airbnb over a forthcoming change that shifts guest fees directly in listing prices. They asked if they should dump their 5% Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) holdings and invest in Toll Brothers. Jim Cramer replied:

Well, I do like Toll Brothers very much, but I have to tell you, I think you're an outlier. As I know, the Jersey beaches, they're always trying to figure out how to stop the party houses; I wouldn't worry. Internationally, Airbnb is smoking it. I say you stay long that stock.

Salesforce (CRM) Stock Surges as Jim Cramer Says AI Fears Were Overstated
Strong Results Support Cramer's Growth Argument

Airbnb, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ABNB) second-quarter revenue rose 17% year over year to $3.6 billion, while gross booking value increased 16% to $27.2 billion and nights and seats booked grew 10% to 148.3 million. Net income reached $816 million, adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $1.3 billion, and free cash flow was about $1.3 billion. Management raised its 2026 outlook to at least 15% revenue growth and an adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5%.

International growth remains important to the thesis. Airbnb reported stronger growth across major markets, while hotel nights are growing about three times faster than its home business. Hotels still account for a single-digit percentage of total nights, but about 35% of first-time guests who book a hotel on Airbnb later return to book a home.

Management also reported a 16% year-over-year decline in customer-support costs per booking, helped by its AI assistant, which resolves nearly 45% of issues that begin with it without human intervention. However, the new 15.5% host-paid fee remains a risk because higher listing prices remains a potential host-retention risk.

Bear Case

The bigger risk is that Airbnb, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ABNB) stock has already priced in much of the recent improvement. Shares closed at $188.07 on August 26, just below the $193.45 52-week high reached on August 24. At that price, it trades at roughly 35 to 36 times forward earnings, based on current market-data estimates. That valuation leaves less room for a slowdown in bookings, margins, or international demand. Furthermore, regulation adds another risk. Short-term-rental restrictions can reduce available listings in individual markets, while hotels and online travel agencies remain significant competitors.

Hedge Fund Ownership Fell, While Short Interest Remains Low

Institutional positioning provides a more cautious signal. According to Insider Monkey, 75 hedge funds held ABNB in the second quarter of 2026, down from 87 in the first quarter. Moreover, Insider Monkey's data shows that over the past few quarters, Harris Associates was the biggest hedge fund shareholder tracked by Insider Monkey with approximately 18.9 million shares in Q2. It is worth noting that short interest offers less evidence of bearish conviction. Multiple market data providers put short interest at roughly 3% of float, and that level indicates limited bearish positioning rather than aggressive speculative bearishness.

Bernstein SocGen Group analyst Richard Clarke just delivered one of Wall Street's more aggressive Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) calls, lifting his price target to $217 from $168 while keeping an Outperform rating. The 29% target increase implies roughly 16% upside from Airbnb's recent $187.30 price, with Clarke arguing that accelerating bookings and strong margins have pushed the company to a clear inflection point.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Sign with ABNB.

Is ABNB fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The call comes after Airbnb posted one of its strongest quarters in years. Second-quarter revenue climbed 17% to $3.6 billion, gross booking value increased 16% to $27.2 billion, and Nights and Seats Booked rose 10%, accelerating from the first quarter. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 21% to $1.3 billion, while margin expanded to 35%.

Clarke sees the booking trajectory as particularly important. Management is guiding toward a fifth consecutive quarter of approximately 10% or higher night growth, suggesting Airbnb may be sustaining a faster growth rate than investors currently expect.

That creates the valuation argument behind Bernstein's upgrade. Clarke estimates Airbnb's current share price embeds medium-term revenue growth of only about 10.5% to 11%. He believes sustained double-digit revenue growth, incremental margin gains and continued buybacks could support approximately 20% annual earnings per share growth.

New businesses could add another layer. Clarke highlighted AI-driven search, dynamic pricing, loyalty programs and sponsored listings as potential long-term growth drivers, including opportunities to improve conversion and create new advertising-style revenue streams.

Investors Takeaway

The biggest test is whether booking growth stays around double digits as comparisons become tougher. Investors should watch Nights and Seats Booked, revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA margins and gross booking value.

Airbnb already showed meaningful acceleration in Q2, but a stock trading near its 52-week high has less room for disappointment.

If bookings remain above 10% growth and new monetization initiatives begin lifting revenue faster than expected, Bernstein's $217 target becomes easier to justify. A slowdown in travel demand or weaker margins would challenge the inflection point thesis.

Does Airbnb Look Undervalued on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) method estimates what Airbnb could be worth based on the cash it is expected to generate for shareholders.
